High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior

sentences.text: Mr. Vivek Kumar Vyas - Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Atul Sharma - Panel Lawyer for respondent/State.

Heard on I.A. No. 7561 of 2023, which is first application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 10.04.2023 passed in SST No.13/2017 by Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, (POCSO Act) Ashoknagar (M.P.) whereby appellant stands convicted under Section 376(2)(i) of the IPC and sentenced him to undergo 10 years RI with a fine of Rs.1,000/-, with default stipulations.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge, (POCSO Act) Ashoknagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted the appellant ignoring the evidence available on record.

He has further argued that as per prosecution story at the time of commission of offence, Kheru(PW/7) came on the spot, however, this witness has totally not supported the case of prosecution and turned hostile.
Even Aunt and father of the prosecutrix have not supported the case of prosecution.
Further argument is that in medical report no sign of rape has been found on the body of the prosecutrix.
The applicant has already suffered one year incarceration out of total maximum sentence awarded to him of 10 years.
Final hearing of this appeal will take long time.
Hence, prayed to suspend the jail sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.
Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on merits of the case, I.A. No. 7561 of 2023 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
